newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Wheat prices rise on rain in edgy Budapest market.
newsitem.headline: Wheat prices rise on rain in edgy Budapest market.

text.p: Hungary's milling wheat futures rebounded on recent rainfall in an uncertain market, traders on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) said on Friday.
"There is a lot of uncertainty in the market," said Robert Vajo of Termin.
Total grains turnover dropped to 963 lots or 444 million forints from Thursday's 1,604 lots or 803 million forints.
Traders said the lower turnover was the result of both active trading on Wednesday and Thursday and the lack of selling for wheat.
"Only one market participant was on the selling side today," said Janos Szolyka of Swap brokerage.
He added that after two days of downward corrections wheat prices continued to rise as the underlying trend remained a rising one.
"I think wheat prices are likely to rise on with the odd corrections," said Szolyka.
Milling wheat prices rose the daily allowed 400 forints per tonne for all maturities until May.
Three new 1998 milling wheat maturities, August, September and October opened today at 24,500, 26,000 and 27,000 forints, respectively.

The wheat market remained uncertain as roughly one third of the crop was yet to be harvested and it was difficult to assess to what extent fears of low quality due to earlier rains were justified, traders said.
"Domestic demand will probably be covered but there will be little milling wheat to export," Szolyka said. "And if there was, current prices are too high for export".
Euro wheat began trading today for all months from August 1998 to January 1999.

Hungarian milling wheat and feed wheat standards are somewhat higher than euro standards and the BCE council decided to start trading for only the 1998 harvest in order not to disturb this year's feed wheat market.
August started at 23,150 forints per tonne, December at 26,000 and January at 27,000 forints.
Maize was steady to higher in minimal turnover as the market continued to focus on milling wheat.
